title: Introduce RAG Katas Lab: compact scenario katas, CLI orchestrator and typed-stubgen
author: Lena Zhao
description: Motivation: onboarding engineers to RAG workflows often requires heavy scaffolding and manual test setup. This PR adds a compact "RAG Katas Lab" quickstart that bundles small, deterministic scenarios (katas), a lightweight CLI orchestrator (rk) for running and replaying sessions, and a typed-stub generator for tool contracts so teams can author tool mocks with TypeScript/Go/py typings. The goal is low-friction, repeatable developer exercises and CI-friendly scenario playback for early-stage integrations. What this PR contains: - three compact katas (intent-disambiguation, index-hiatus, streaming-tool-fallback) with preseeded corpora and minimal index configs - rk CLI: run, replay, record, and snapshot commands + a --seed flag for deterministic tokenization - typed-stubgen: scans a tool-contract.json and emits typed stubs (ts/go/py) and a tiny adapter shim for local testing - structured-output linter hooks: an eslint-like runner that validates schema/contract conformance against snapshoted outputs - docs: quickstart readme, workshop guide, and docs-site nav entry - small telemetry probes: optional probes that emit structured trace points for step boundaries (disabled by default) Usage (examples): 1) bootstrap: git clone ... && cd redwood-quickstarts/examples/rag-katas && make deps 2) run kata: rk run --kata intent-disambiguation --index local/sample.index --model redwood/ada-compat 3) record a session: rk record --kata streaming-tool-fallback --out ./snapshots/streaming-1.json 4) generate typed stubs: stubgen --contract examples/contracts/calc-tool-contract.json --lang ts --out examples/stubs/ The PR includes a compact checklist: - [x] kata scenarios and corpora - [x] rk CLI (run/replay/record) + README - [x] typed-stubgen + examples - [x] structured-output-lint integration for CI - [x] docs site entry and workshop guide - [x] basic unit tests and smoke CI compatibility Backwards compatibility and scope: everything is additive, feature-flagged by default (rk is in examples/ and not wired into production CI), and the typed stubs are opt-in. Related: ENG-1298 (developer onboarding), PM-402 (quickstart content plan).
